chapter.title: Nuclear Reactors, Boilers, Machinery and Mechanical Appliances; Parts Thereof

page.h1: HTS Chapter 84: Nuclear Reactors, Boilers, Machinery and Mechanical Appliances; Parts Thereof — Foreign Tariff Changes on U.S. Exports

seo.title: Foreign Tariff Changes on U.S. Machinery Since 2025 (HTS Ch. 84) | KoalaGains
seo.shortDescription: Every tariff change other countries made on U.S. machinery since January 2025: China's extra duties and farm-machinery list, Canada's surtax list, the EU zero tariff and pending Taiwan and India deals.
keywords: China tariff on US farm machinery

intro: Three actions cost U.S. machinery exporters money today: China's 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods (since May 2025), China's further 10% on agricultural machinery (since February 2025) and Canada's 15–50% surtax on about 50 machinery tariff items (since September 8, 2026). Everything else has moved the other way or not yet moved: the EU cut its remaining tariffs to zero on July 1, 2026, and Taiwan and India have promised cuts that are not in force. The two dates to watch are China's — exclusions from its 2019 tariffs end December 31, 2026, and the suspension of 24 points of its extra duty ends January 10, 2027.
scope: The 9 largest markets for U.S. Chapter 84 goods (78% of 2025 exports).

upcoming.title: China's tariff exclusions for U.S. goods end
upcoming.whatHappens: China's exclusions from its 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods are valid until December 31, 2026 under the November 2025 U.S.–China deal.
upcoming.impact: If China does not extend the exclusions, the 2019 counter-tariffs they lift would apply again to the covered U.S. machinery lines, on top of China's MFN rate and the 10% extra duties. Which Chapter 84 lines are excluded must be checked line by line in the Chinese notices.

upcoming.title: China's suspension of 24 points of its extra tariff on U.S. goods ends
upcoming.whatHappens: China suspended 24 points of its extra tariff on all U.S. goods for one year from November 10, 2025, keeping 10%. In September 2026 the two sides agreed to extend the arrangement to January 10, 2027, with talks on a further extension expected before the end of the year.
upcoming.impact: If the suspension lapses on January 10, 2027, China's extra duty on all U.S. goods would rise from 10% to 34%. U.S. refrigerating equipment would go from 19% to 43% and harvesting machinery from 28% to 52%.
upcoming.status: Extension to Jan 10, 2027 announced by MOFCOM; China's Tariff Commission has not yet published its notice

inEffect.measure: Extra tariff on all U.S. goods cut to 10%
inEffect.appliesTo: Every Chapter 84 good, on top of China's normal rate (8% on harvesting machinery (8433) and 9% on refrigerators and heat pumps (8418) in the WITS sample; other headings differ).
inEffect.whatItMeans: A $1,000,000 shipment of U.S. refrigerating equipment (China MFN 9%) pays about $190,000 in duty now against $90,000 in January 2025.

inEffect.appliesTo: 40-odd Chapter 84 lines in Annex 2 of Announcement 2025 No. 1 — crop-drying and food-processing machines, sprayers, soil-preparation and harvesting machinery, milking and dairy machines, poultry and farm machines and grain-cleaning machines. The 10% is added to China's MFN rate and to the 10% extra duty on all U.S. goods.
inEffect.whatItMeans: $1,000,000 of U.S. harvesting machinery (China MFN 8%) paid $80,000 in January 2025; it now pays $280,000 (8% + 10% + 10%).

inEffect.measure: Counter-tariffs on U.S. products (answering U.S. Section 338 tariffs)
inEffect.appliesTo: About 50 Chapter 84 tariff items on Canada's September 2026 list: 15% on air conditioners, lifting and handling equipment, parts, harvesting machinery and moulds; 25% on pumps, compressors, refrigerators, packaging machinery, washers, dryers and hand tools; 50% on refrigerated display units. Most machinery is not listed.
inEffect.whatItMeans: $100,000 of listed U.S. refrigerators (8418) that entered free under CUSMA now pays $25,000; listed air conditioners (8415) pay $15,000. The surtax has no CUSMA exemption, and unlisted lines in the same headings are not affected.

changes.title: U.S.–China Board of Trade product lists
changes.status: Recommended for reduced tariffs; no Chinese tariff cut published yet
changes.detail: China's import list under the U.S.–China Board of Trade “30-for-30” framework names 1,619 Chinese tariff lines that could get lower tariffs on U.S. goods. No Chinese tariff cut has been published yet. Non-seed soybeans (Chapter 12's dominant export) were explicitly excluded from this list; the 10% extra tariff stays on them. For Chapter 84 it names 12 lines: pumps (8413.60, 8413.70), vacuum pumps (8414.10), medical and laboratory sterilizers (8419.20), water filtering machines (8421.21), valves and valve parts (8481, 8481.90) and transmission parts (8483.90). No Chinese tariff cut has been published.

changes.title: Counter-tariffs on U.S. products (answering U.S. Section 338 tariffs)
changes.detail: Counter-tariffs of 15%, 25% and 50% on listed U.S. products — steel, aluminum, dairy, furniture and clothing, but also machinery, household appliances and electronics such as smartphones, routers and monitors (50%). The order applies to goods of U.S. origin and has no exemption for goods that qualify for CUSMA. For Chapter 84 the list reaches about 50 tariff items: at 15% air conditioners (8415), lifting and handling equipment (8427, 8428), parts (8431), harvesting machinery (8433) and moulds (8480); at 25% pumps and compressors (8413, 8414), refrigerators and freezers (8418), packaging machinery (8422), washers and dryers (8450, 8451) and hand tools (8467); at 50% refrigerated display units (8418.50). The surtax has no CUSMA exemption.

changes.title: Brazil has imposed nothing on U.S. goods; it is challenging U.S. tariffs at the WTO
changes.status: Nothing imposed on U.S. goods; talks ongoing
changes.detail: Brazil has published no countermeasure on U.S. goods. Its Economic Reciprocity Law (Law 15,122 of April 11, 2025) would allow them — such as import restrictions or suspending intellectual-property obligations — but none has been applied. On July 27, 2026 Brazil asked the United States for WTO consultations over U.S. tariffs on Brazilian goods, and Brazilian ministers met USTR on August 31 and September 30, 2026 to set up a working group on a possible agreement.

changes.title: EU extends suspension of its Boeing/Airbus-dispute retaliatory tariffs on U.S. goods
changes.status: Suspended since July 11, 2021; extended by Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1549 from July 11, 2026
changes.detail: The U.S. and EU suspended, for five years from July 11, 2021, the tariffs each had imposed or threatened in their 17-year WTO dispute over Boeing and Airbus subsidies (the EU's WTO-authorized countermeasures covered up to $4 billion of U.S. goods, large civil aircraft among them, under the Cooperative Framework for Large Civil Aircraft). Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1549 of July 6, 2026 extends the EU's suspension past its July 10, 2026 expiry; the U.S. has not reactivated its Section 301 tariffs from the same dispute either.

changes.title: USMCA stays in force: Canada and Mexico keep 0% on qualifying U.S. goods
changes.detail: At the first USMCA joint review on July 1, 2026 the three countries did not agree to a new 16-year term, so the agreement is now reviewed every year; it stays in force until at least July 1, 2036. Canada and Mexico keep applying USMCA rates to qualifying U.S. goods.

changes.title: EU–U.S. framework tariff cuts adopted
changes.detail: Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 cuts EU duties on listed U.S. goods to zero from July 1, 2026, and Regulation (EU) 2026/1461 sets aside duties on certain other goods. Annex I of Regulation (EU) 2026/1455 lists Chapter 84 in full, so the EU's remaining tariffs on machinery fall to zero from July 1, 2026, through December 31, 2029; the Commission can suspend the cut.

changes.title: U.S.–Taiwan Agreement on Reciprocal Trade: Taiwan to eliminate or reduce tariff barriers on U.S. goods
changes.status: Signed; takes effect after both sides finish domestic steps (Taiwan's legislature must review it)
changes.detail: Under the USTR fact sheet, Taiwan will give preferential market access to U.S. industrial exports including machinery, autos, chemicals and electrical products, eliminating or reducing 99% of tariff barriers. No Taiwanese tariff cut has been published yet.

changes.title: U.S.–Bangladesh Agreement on Reciprocal Trade: Bangladesh sets purchase goals for U.S. wheat, soy, cotton and LNG
changes.detail: Bangladesh endeavors to buy about $3.5 billion of U.S. farm goods, including wheat (at least 700,000 tonnes a year for five years), soy and cotton, and about $15 billion of U.S. energy over 15 years, including long-term LNG contracts, and agrees to accept U.S. sanitary and phytosanitary certificates. The U.S. keeps a 19% rate on most Bangladeshi goods. The agreement sets purchase goals and does not itself change Bangladesh's tariffs on U.S. goods.

changes.title: U.S.–India framework: India to eliminate or reduce tariffs on U.S. industrial goods
changes.status: Framework announced; no implementing Indian tariff notification found
changes.detail: The February 6, 2026 U.S.–India joint statement says India will eliminate or reduce tariffs on all U.S. industrial goods. It gives no effective date, and we found no Indian notification implementing it.

changes.title: Mexico raises its general tariffs on goods from countries without a trade agreement
changes.status: In force since Jan 1, 2026; U.S. goods still enter under USMCA
changes.detail: The decree raises Mexico's general (MFN) rates on more than 1,400 tariff lines, mostly cars, textiles, clothing, steel, plastics and footwear. U.S. goods that qualify for USMCA keep their preferential rate. Mexico has published no counter-tariff on U.S. goods.

changes.title: Reciprocity petition against the 2025 U.S. tariffs: framing approved, action deferred
changes.detail: Camex's executive committee (Gecex) approved the Foreign Ministry's petition as falling under the Economic Reciprocity Law and chose to await diplomatic consultations before forming the working group that would propose countermeasures. Nothing was imposed.

changes.title: U.S.–UK pharmaceutical pricing arrangement
changes.status: In force; full text agreed Apr 2, 2026
changes.detail: Not a tariff: the UK raises the net price it pays for new medicines by about 25% and lifts NICE’s cost-effectiveness threshold. UK tariffs on medicines stay at zero.

changes.title: U.S.–Switzerland–Liechtenstein trade framework
changes.detail: Switzerland intends to apply zero duties on all U.S. industrial goods. Switzerland's zero-duty treatment of industrial goods includes machinery, so Chapter 84 is covered.

changes.title: China extends its tariff exclusions for U.S. goods to December 31, 2026
changes.detail: Under the November 2025 U.S.–China deal, China extended its market-based exclusion process for imports from the United States; exclusions stay valid until December 31, 2026. They lift China's 2019 counter-tariffs on U.S. goods (answering the U.S. Section 301 tariffs), which were never repealed. Whether a given Chapter 84 line is excluded depends on the line; the 2019 counter-tariffs that exclusions lift are listed in Annex 3 of the Chinese notices.

changes.title: U.S.–Japan agreement
changes.detail: Executive Order 14345 implements the U.S.–Japan agreement: Japan works toward buying U.S. farm and other goods worth $8 billion a year and investing in the U.S.

changes.title: EU countermeasures on about €93B of U.S. goods
changes.detail: Implementing Regulation (EU) 2025/1564 listed about €93B of U.S. goods for extra duties from September 7, 2025. The measures were suspended from August 6, 2025, again from February 7, 2026, and from August 7, 2026 with no end date (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1893). The Commission described the target list of its March 2025 package as including home appliances and house tools among its industrial goods; the consolidated package is suspended with no end date (Implementing Regulation (EU) 2026/1893) and has never been applied. The annex lines were not retrievable for this review, so product-level coverage is not confirmed.

changes.title: China imposes anti-dumping duties of up to 74.9% on U.S. polyoxymethylene (POM) copolymer
changes.status: In force from 2025-05-19 for five years (deposits from 2025-01-24)
changes.detail: MOFCOM Announcement No. 25 of 2025 (final ruling of 2025-05-18): anti-dumping duties on POM copolymer (HS 3907.1010 and 3907.1090) from the U.S., EU, Taiwan and Japan. The rate for all U.S. companies, including Ticona Polymers, is 74.9%. It is a trade-remedy case, not a general counter-tariff, and covers only this one resin.

changes.title: Extra tariff on all U.S. goods cut to 10%
changes.status: In force; 24-point suspension extended to Jan 10, 2027
changes.detail: Rose 34% → 84% → 125% in April 2025 (125% from April 12), then cut to 10% from May 14, 2025 with 24 points suspended for 90 days. The suspension was extended for 90 days from August 12, 2025 and for one year from November 10, 2025, with the 10% kept. In September 2026 the two sides agreed to extend the arrangement to January 10, 2027. Applies to every U.S.-origin good on top of China’s normal rate.

changes.title: U.S.–UK Economic Prosperity Deal
changes.detail: UK concessions were a beef quota and a duty-free ethanol quota.

changes.title: 25% surtax on U.S. passenger vehicles and light trucks (non-U.S. content for CUSMA-compliant vehicles)
changes.now: 25% on non-U.S. content (full value if not CUSMA-compliant)
changes.status: In force; kept when Canada removed most 2025 counter-tariffs on Sept 1, 2025
changes.detail: Canada's United States Surtax Order (Motor Vehicles 2025), SOR/2025-118: a 25% surtax on U.S. passenger vehicles and light trucks (8703, 8704). A CUSMA-compliant vehicle pays it only on its non-U.S. content; a non-compliant vehicle pays on its full value. Auto parts are not covered.

changes.title: China's extra tariffs of 10% and 15% on U.S. farm goods, lifted November 10, 2025
changes.detail: Tariff Commission Announcement No. 2 of 2025 (March 4) added 15% on U.S. chicken, wheat, corn and cotton and 10% on sorghum, soybeans, pork, beef, aquatic products, fruits, vegetables and dairy from March 10, 2025, answering the U.S. fentanyl tariffs. Announcement No. 9 of 2025 (November 5) stopped them from November 10, 2025, under the U.S.–China deal. China's separate extra tariff on all U.S. goods stays.

changes.title: 25% counter-tariff on C$30B of U.S. goods
changes.detail: 25% counter-tariff on C$30B of U.S. goods. Canada repealed most of it on Sept 1, 2025, keeping only the steel, aluminum and auto surtaxes. None of the surviving orders (steel, aluminum, motor vehicles) lists a Chapter 84 item.

changes.title: Extra 10% on U.S. agricultural machinery, larger-engine cars and pickups (and 15% on coal and LNG)
changes.status: In force (MOFCOM's policy database lists the announcement as currently effective)
changes.detail: China's State Council Tariff Commission (Announcement 2025 No. 1, issued February 4, 2025) put an extra 10% on U.S. agricultural machinery from February 10, 2025. Annex 2 lists 40-odd Chapter 84 lines: crop-drying and food-processing machines (8419.33, 8419.34, 8438.60), sprayers (8424.41, .49, .82), soil-preparation and harvesting machinery (8432, 8433), milking and dairy machines (8434), poultry and farm machines (8436), grain-cleaning machines (8437) and 8479.20. The November 2025 deal lifted China's March 2025 farm-product tariffs; we found no notice lifting these.
